Faisalabad-Based PakCem Appoints New CEO Amid Industry Growth

Faisalabad: PakCem Industries, a leading player in Pakistan’s construction materials sector, announced on Tuesday the appointment of Farooq Ahmed Khan as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective July 1. The decision comes as the company seeks to further strengthen its position in a market experiencing steady growth in infrastructure and urban development.

Mr. Khan, previously Chief Operating Officer at PakCem, brings over 25 years of experience in the construction materials industry to his new role. He succeeds Imran Siddiqui, who led the company for the past eight years and is retiring after a distinguished career. At a press conference held at the company’s Faisalabad headquarters, Khan outlined his immediate priorities: “My focus will be on enhancing operational efficiency, expanding our product range, and supporting the government’s vision for affordable housing and infrastructure development. PakCem is committed to contributing to Pakistan’s progress.”

The appointment has been welcomed by industry observers and trade associations. Tanveer Shah, President of the Pakistan Construction Materials Association, remarked, “Mr. Khan’s deep understanding of both manufacturing and market dynamics makes him an excellent choice. The industry’s steady demand, especially from major infrastructure projects like highways, dams, and residential schemes, means strong leadership at companies like PakCem is crucial.”

The construction materials sector in Pakistan has posted a growth rate of around 6% over the last fiscal year, driven by continued investment in public and private sector projects. Analysts note that while the sector faces challenges such as fluctuating input costs and logistics bottlenecks, it remains a key contributor to the national economy, accounting for an estimated 10% of industrial GDP.

“PakCem’s leadership transition is timely,” said Anam Riaz, an Islamabad-based construction analyst. “There is increasing competition in the market, with new entrants and innovations in cement and related materials. It will be important for established companies to stay agile and focus on quality and customer service.”

PakCem Industries employs over 1,200 people across its manufacturing facilities in Punjab and Sindh. The company’s products are widely used in housing developments, commercial buildings, and public infrastructure. Company officials highlighted ongoing investments in technology upgrades and skills training as part of their commitment to sustainable growth.

Outgoing CEO Imran Siddiqui expressed confidence in his successor: “Farooq has been instrumental in PakCem’s journey and is well-placed to take the company to new heights.”

Trade unions representing PakCem workers also greeted the announcement positively. “We look forward to continued engagement with management under Mr. Khan’s leadership,” said Riaz Hussain, spokesperson for the PakCem Employees Federation.

With this appointment, PakCem signals its intent to maintain a leading role in supporting Pakistan’s construction boom.
